source_text: Cuba appears to be tottering toward some kind of political transition. Some Cubans are concerned that the residents own nothing and are too impoverished to take over the few functioning businesses on the island, while there is a large and wealthy diaspora community (and potentially also foreign investors) who would be able to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices.
rewritten_text: Look at what decades of failed socialist stagnation have brought to Cuba—a nation now tottering toward a desperate political transition. The tragic reality of absolute state control is that the hardworking people on the ground own nothing and have been reduced to impoverishment, stripped of personal responsibility and the chance to build generational security. And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this breakdown of social order? A wealthy diaspora and foreign investors ready to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices, sweeping aside the cultural continuity of the homeland. This is what happens when traditional bonds and stable, orderly governance are eroded by radical experiments. Without a firm grounding in property ownership and true self-reliance, the local population is left entirely vulnerable to outside economic forces.

The hardworking people on the ground in Cuba have been stripped of ownership and left in impoverishment, and now the nation is brought to the brink of a desperate political transition. Absolute state control destroys the chance for families to build generational security. And what is the inevitable result? A wealthy diaspora and foreign investors are waiting in the wings to swoop in and buy up property and businesses at bargain prices, destroying the cultural continuity of the homeland. Without a firm grounding in property ownership and true self-reliance, the local population is left entirely vulnerable to these outside economic forces. It is a stark warning of what happens when you let radical experiments erode traditional bonds and orderly rule.
